% Pattern: head/wrapper. The paper defines a command for each kind, with two
% optional arguments for the title and the label, that puts its last argument
% in the environment. A call is the environment, and a \label in the body of
% the definition is the label of the call. Seen in the gold pilot (set E).
% want lemma-1 statement/lemma 1 labels=lem.one
% want claim-1 statement/claim 1.1
% want proof-1 proof - proves=lemma-1
% want definition-1 definition 2 labels=def.two
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{amsthm,xargs}
\newtheorem{lemma}{Lemma}
\newtheorem{definition}[lemma]{Definition}
\newtheorem{claim}{Claim}[lemma]
\newcommandtwoopt{\lemm}[3][][]{
  \begin{lemma}[#1]\label{#2}
    #3
  \end{lemma}}
\newcommandtwoopt{\defi}[3][][]{
  \begin{definition}[#1]\label{#2}
    #3$\hfill\dashv$
  \end{definition}}
\newcommand{\clai}[2][]{\begin{claim}[#1]#2\end{claim}}
\begin{document}
\section{One}
Some text before.

\lemm[Small][lem.one]{
Every compact space is bounded.
\clai{The cover has a finite part.}
}
\begin{proof}
Cover the space by balls.
\end{proof}

\defi[][def.two]{A space is nice when it is compact.}
\end{document}
